subject.title: fix(irc): disconnect on oversized inbound lines

question: Should an oversized inbound IRC record be discarded with bounded state, or should it disconnect and enter an explicit supervised reconnect/backoff lifecycle?
rationale: Both responses are protocol-permitted, but the current passive monitor does not recover from a post-ready socket close, so the choice determines whether malformed input requires operator intervention.

options.title: Discard Oversized Record
options.body: Enter a bounded discard-until-delimiter state, report the violation once, and prove the next legal record is processed.

options.title: Disconnect And Reconnect
options.body: Keep fail-closed socket closure but propagate it through the account lifecycle and add supervised reconnect/backoff proof.

options.title: Accept Manual Recovery
options.body: Merge as written with explicit acceptance that one malformed record can require an account or gateway restart.

recommendation.title: Discard Oversized Record
recommendation.body: Enter a bounded discard-until-delimiter state, report the violation once, and prove the next legal record is processed.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR timeline shows direct engagement with this IRC change and the unresolved choice is channel lifecycle policy rather than a mechanical edit.
